idiom_name: sealed interface + data class variants + exhaustive when
implementation_notes: Sealed interfaces (Kotlin 1.5+) close the hierarchy: every direct subtype is known at compile time, so a when over a sealed subject is required to be exhaustive and the else branch can be omitted. Data classes supply value equality, toString and copy for the product half, data objects cover payload-free variants, and destructuring declarations work directly in when branches. Nothing is hand-written: the dispatcher is an expression and a missing variant is a compile error.
code_sketch:
sealed interface Shape
data class Circle(val radius: Double) : Shape
data class Square(val side: Double) : Shape

fun area(shape: Shape): Double = when (shape) {
    is Circle -> Math.PI * shape.radius * shape.radius
    is Square -> shape.side * shape.side
}   // exhaustive; no else needed
pitfalls: Sealed subclasses must be declared in the same package and module, which also means a Java source file inside that module can still add an implementation - the closure is module-scoped, not file-scoped.
In multiplatform common code an else branch is still required, because platform-specific actual declarations may add subtypes unknown to the common source set.
A non-exhaustive when used as a statement is a compiler error for sealed subjects on modern Kotlin; relying on an old compiler or a stray else silently drops coverage.
data class copy() creates a new instance - equality is structural, so identity checks (===) and caches keyed by reference do not behave like the variant values they hold.
